items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: the percussion leader, Sgt. Wadkowicz, he dragged me right into that room. ... I now was into the New York Army band.

ctx.x: By the way, he happened to have been a war hero believe it or not. I mean you wouldn’t think so, you know, Mr. Peepers. So now I said, “how was that.” He said, “next.” You know like, he kept going down the line, man, instead of go to the back of the line like Herman Slabonski had to go to the back of the line and start over. So now I get down to © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

the final table with the guys with the stamp. And I said I had to have failed, you know. He takes this stamp, I thought he was going to break the table. Bang! Fully qualified for military service. I said, “oh my God.” Here we go man. I mean even my eyes. I mean I used to wear glasses. I had 20/200 vision, a couple surgeries and cataract surgery, I’m 20/20 now you know, except I have to use reading glasses. So anyway, we get back up to Cortland, now my father owned a bar around the corner called the Crystal Hotel.…
